## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e7586a892e7b02bef5d0635f616d15070c45e8a7`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #21259 (body, claim 5942590152, os-dev-report 5943202786), PR #21272 (body, 3-file list, three-dot diff against merge base `8dea55d3`, which is byte-identical to GitHub's diff: +262/-0), the head's files read with `git show`, and the head's check-runs read last. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Registry `undeclaredAuditTimestampFields` — right.** Installed in `registerManagedObjectMetadata`, the one seam both managed doors pass through: `initObjects` calls `registerObjectMetadata` as its first step, and a `skipSchemaSync` boot calls `registerObjectMetadata` and stops. It is keyed by the same `tableName` the sibling coercion registries (`datetimeFields`, `dateFields`, `jsonFields`) use, so `formatInput(object, …)` resolves it exactly as it resolves the declared-datetime set. The entry is a filter over `AUDIT_TIMESTAMP_COLUMNS` (two names) by non-declaration: nothing else can enter it.

2. **The `formatInput` arm — right on every write door.** All six `formatInput` call sites in the driver are managed-object write doors: `create`, `update`, `upsert`, `bulkCreate`, `updateMany`, and `rotatedUpdateById` (the shard branch of `update`, which the PR body does not name but which inherits the fix because it formats before it stamps). The arm runs after the declared-datetime arm and before the date/time arms, skips `null`/`undefined`, and calls `storageDatetimeValue`, the identical function a declared `Field.datetime` takes: `canonicalUtcDatetime` (core's `temporalStorageForm`) renders a parseable value as canonical text and hands an unparseable one back untouched, and `mysqlDatetimeLiteral` rewrites only an exactly-canonical string. So nothing new can be silently reinterpreted; junk still fails loudly at the server. The remaining `.insert`/`.update` sites in the file are the driver's own tables (the sequences table, the lock key, the widening rewrite), not object rows. The driver's own stamps are untouched and were never the producer: `stampInsertTimestamps` (SQLite only, ISO text) and `updatedAtStamp` (ISO text on SQLite, `now(3)`/`now()` raw elsewhere) are applied after `formatInput`, so the caller's text reaches MySQL only under `preserveAudit`, which is exactly the path the update/updateMany pins exercise.

3. **Bounded to managed objects' audit columns — right.** A declared column of any type is excluded ("the declaration wins"), consistent with the read side's audit arm in `readPresentationKind`. External objects are excluded in fact, not by comment: `registerExternalObject` writes none of this map, so the lookup is `undefined` and the arm is skipped, and `initObjects` is `assertSchemaMutable`-gated so a federated datasource cannot reach the managed registration at all. Residual, not a defect: a managed object registered DDL-free over a hand-migrated table lacking the column gets an entry, but the arm only formats a value the caller supplied, and a write naming a missing column fails exactly as before.

4. **Recompute per registration — right.** The entry is assigned, not merged, so a re-registration that now declares the column drops it. The inverse edge (a declaration later removed) leaves the pre-existing additive `datetimeFields` set and the new entry both naming the column; both arms apply one idempotent function (a naive MySQL spelling is read as UTC and re-rendered byte-identically), so the double pass is a no-op.

5. **The producer, and the fix site — right.** At the head, `packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts` `applyToRecord` sets `record.updated_at` to `new Date().toISOString()` on every insert and update unconditionally, its own docblock stating the premise: driver-sql creates both columns on every table. The better-auth jwks schema carries no `updatedAt`, so the adapter is not the producer; the dev's measurement matches the code. The VALUE is the platform's canonical instant; the REFUSED LITERAL is produced at the driver's bind, the layer that chose `DATETIME(3)` for the column it provisioned. Fixing the driver's write formatting is therefore the producer-side fix the card asked for and not a per-caller workaround: declaring `updated_at` on `sys_jwks` would close 1 of the 11 objects the census found (9 `created_at`-only, 2 neither), while this closes all 11 and every future `managedBy: 'better-auth'` / `systemFields: false` object. The opt-out rows are confirmed in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts` (`applySystemFields`: "the two opt-out rows (`systemFields: false`, `managedBy: 'better-auth'`)").

6. **The SQLite storage-form delta — `Clause-②: no` is right.** The accept set does not move: a JS `Date` written to an undeclared audit column was accepted before and still is. What moves is the stored form of that one input on one dialect, from an epoch INTEGER that read back as a number (`presentAuditTimestampOutput` passes non-strings through, ADR-0074's "total" rule) to the canonical text, which is the shape ADR-0053 D-F1 already rules for the audit stamps at every read door on every dialect. No reader depended on the integer form: a grep over `packages/**` and `examples/**` for a numeric reading of `created_at`/`updated_at` finds none, and every in-tree producer of an undeclared audit value writes text (the engine hook, the driver's stamps, REST's JSON); the one direct-driver fixture that writes a `Date` (`sql-driver-11176-bulk-and-merge-updated-at.test.ts` §2) deliberately sends text on SQLite. Not a `(narrowing)` either. Residual, outside this card: a row ALREADY holding an INTEGER in an undeclared audit column on SQLite still reads back as a number, since the audit read repair does not fold numbers; its measured producer set is empty, so I note it rather than escalate it.

7. **The pins and the ablation — they prove what they claim, with PostgreSQL as the control.** One cell per dialect through `declareDialectCell`, so an unprovisioned live cell is declared and is fatal under the matrix expectation flag. CI's required `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` job runs the WHOLE driver-sql suite under `TZ=America/New_York` with both server URLs and that flag, so the new file runs live in a required job; that job is `success` on this head. The assertions read the driver's actual bind through knex `query` events rather than inferring it from a read-back: the MySQL literal on MySQL plus `not.toContain` of the ISO text, the hook's text byte-identical on SQLite and PostgreSQL, read-back equality through `findOne` on all five doors, the `Date` case, and a shape guard proving the fixture really is undeclared (`declaredFieldsFor`, `datetimeFields`, `columnInfo`). The reported before-fix run (6 failed: 5 live MySQL plus the SQLite `Date` case, PostgreSQL 0) and the ablation at the committed head (registry read replaced by `undefined`: 7 failed, the same six MySQL doors now including `updateMany` plus the SQLite `Date` case, PostgreSQL 0, restore proven by blob identity) are the dev's readings, not re-run here, and their direction is what the diff predicts. PostgreSQL is a genuine control: it parses the canonical text natively and binds a `Date` as a timestamp, so it is green with and without the arm, which is what makes MySQL's six and SQLite's one attributable to the arm and nothing else.

8. **Untouched, confirmed.** The 42 lines added to `sql-driver.ts` are a documented field declaration, five lines in `registerManagedObjectMetadata` and twenty-two in `formatInput`; `nowColumnDefault` and `migrateMysqlDatetimeColumns` are not in the diff. `sys-jwks.object.ts` is not in the file list, so its key-material fields are untouched, and no `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/**` path is touched. `SqliteWasmDriver` and `TursoDriver` extend `SqlDriver` and override none of `formatInput`, `registerManagedObjectMetadata` or `storageDatetimeValue` (Turso's remote path calls `this.formatInput`), so the arm reaches both inheritors unchanged, matching the dev's suite runs.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/21259-undeclared-audit-timestamp-mysql.md`: `@objectstack/driver-sql` `patch` — right. The package is published (`version` 17.5.0, no `private` flag) and this is a bug fix in it. `Clause-②: no` stands at line start in the changeset (line 7) and in the PR body (line 3); no direction arm is owed. The prose is accurate against the code: the driver creates both columns on every table it builds (`initObjects` and `ensureShardTable` both call `createAuditTimestampColumn` twice), the engine stamps both as ISO text, only a declared `Field.datetime` was rewritten, the two opt-out rows are the registry's, and the five named doors all format the column (the rotation branch of `update` too). The SQLite paragraph states the storage-form delta and its direction correctly. On public surface: the one added member is `protected` on an exported class, additive, not an accept set and not a documented API, so the `no` holds.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Deviation 1 (PR assignee empty).** Confirmed: #21272 has no assignee. The dev's `label-write --assign` was denied by its local permission layer before any network call and was not routed around, which is the right conduct. Not a diff matter; the seat sets it.
- **Deviation 2 (hygiene slip).** About 150 hex characters of a throwaway key's ciphertext were printed into the dev's own session transcript only; the key never persisted (0 rows; database dropped). I swept the diff, the PR body, both comment threads and the card for hex runs of 48 or more characters, base64-shaped runs of 64 or more, and PEM markers: zero hex and PEM hits; the four long-token hits are three file paths and one API URL. Nothing posted carries key material. Noted; nothing for the diff.
- **Deviation 3 (temp dirs).** Server dirs under `/tmp/os21259-*` for the postgres-user traversal and the socket-path limit, removed; every server stopped by recorded pid. Not a diff matter. Noted.
- **The auth-logger finding.** Filed by the seat as #21274 (open; positions in `objectql` and `plugin-auth`; classes and positions only, no values). The PR body's "reported for the seat to file" is discharged. The path remains and is outside this card.
- **Acceptance note, filters.** The filter comparand path (`coerceFilterValue` through `temporalFieldKind`) has no undeclared-audit arm, so a canonical `…Z` comparand on an undeclared audit column reaches MySQL unrewritten; the dev measured `$gt` and equality answering the right rows on live MySQL. Judged: pre-existing, outside the card's write-door scope, and measured rather than assumed. It holds because MySQL's comparison-context parse tolerates the ISO text where its strict-mode INSERT does not; a later card could extend the write/filter symmetry to the audit columns rather than rely on that. Noted, not blocking.
- **Acceptance note, the #11176 fixture.** Its §2 `Date` on PostgreSQL/MySQL now passes through the new arm as the same instant, its SQLite leg sends text and is unchanged, and the dev reports the whole driver-sql suite green with both live servers. Leaving it untouched is right for scope; it could drop its dialect switch in a later hygiene pass.
- **The `sys_activity` note.** #21241 has since landed on `main` through PR #21252, after this branch's base. GitHub reports #21272 mergeable; the two `sql-driver.ts` regions are disjoint (`nowColumnDefault` / `migrateMysqlDatetimeColumns` against `registerManagedObjectMetadata` / `formatInput`), and the queue rebuilds onto current `main`. The note was accurate when written and is resolved upstream.
- **`open_questions`:** empty; nothing to answer.
- **Escalated to the seat, not a FAIL: the door pin.** The card asked for a MySQL live cell in which JWT signing succeeds and `GET /api/v1/auth/jwks` answers 200. The PR delivers a driver pin of record on all three dialects plus a one-off door measurement (MySQL before and after; PostgreSQL and SQLite after only), stating its reason (no live-dialect harness boots `plugin-auth`) and citing a precedent on #21227 that is outside this brief's inputs and was not read. The door's 200 is a reported reading, not a test of record; the seat confirms the precedent applies. The defect's own layer is pinned in a required job and the end-to-end claim was measured once, so the record passes on the diff.
- **`Fixes #21259`** is the right keyword: the class is closed, the pins and changeset are in, and the log finding is its own card.
- **Check-runs on this head.** Read at 2026-10-02T00:31Z: 32 check-runs, 23 `success`, 3 `skipped` by path filter (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke), 6 `in_progress`, 0 failures; the one legacy status is `success`. Of the seven required contexts, `Build Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` are `success`; `Lint & Repo Gates` is in progress, and the `Test Core` and `TypeScript Type Check` rollups have not reported yet (four `Test Core` shards and the `Type Check · workspace` leg are still running; the other `Test Core` shards and `Type Check · consumer gates`, `debt ledger` and `source gates` are `success`). An in-progress required job is not yet a verdict: the seat confirms the green bar itself before enqueue.
